merger_description:
Accenture Venture Holdings, LLC, an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of Accenture plc (together with its direct and indirect subsidiaries, **Accenture**) proposes to acquire approximately 80% to 90% of the shares in (and control of) Dragos, Inc. (together with its direct and indirect subsidiaries, including Phosphorus Security LLC (**Phosphorus**), **Dragos**).

Accenture is a global professional services company headquartered in Dublin, Ireland. It provides a broad range of services across strategy, consulting, digital, technology, and operations designed to assist public and private clients.

Accenture provides a range of services in the cybersecurity space from strategic planning through managed security services, operating as both a strategic consultant and systems integrator, working with technology solution partners to offer full-service offerings to customers.

Dragos is a global supplier of Operational Technology (**OT**) cybersecurity asset discovery, vulnerability management and threat detection technology, as well as threat intelligence and related services. Its subsidiary, Phosphorus, provides extended Internet of Things (**xIoT**) device discovery, vulnerability identification and remediation technology. Dragos is headquartered in the US.

Accenture has separately notified its proposed acquisition of runZero, Inc (MN-60031), which the ACCC is also assessing.

events.title: Accenture - Dragos - Phase 1 Determination

determination_table_content.details:
Accenture Venture Holdings, LLC, an indirect wholly-owned
subsidiary of Accenture plc (together with its direct and indirect
subsidiaries, Accenture) proposes to acquire approximately 80% to
90% of the shares in (and control of) Dragos, Inc. (together with its
direct and indirect subsidiaries, including Phosphorus Security LLC
(Phosphorus)) (Dragos) (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Accenture, is a global professional services company
headquartered in Dublin, Ireland. It provides a broad range of
services across strategy, consulting, digital, technology, and
operations designed to assist public and private clients. Accenture
provides a range of services in the cybersecurity space including
strategic planning through managed security services and operating
as a strategic consultant and systems integrator, working with
technology solution partners to offer full-service offerings to
customers.
The target, Dragos, is a global supplier of Operational Technology
(OT) cybersecurity asset discovery, vulnerability management and
threat detection technology, as well as threat intelligence and related
services. Its subsidiary, Phosphorus, provides extended Internet of
Things (xIoT) device discovery, vulnerability identification and
remediation technology. Dragos is headquartered in the US.
The Parties overlap in the supply of OT cybersecurity services.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
Acquisition notification form, information from third parties and
other information available to it. The ACCC notes that it also
received a separate and concurrent notification of Accenture’s
proposed acquisition of 100% of the shares in runZero, Inc (MN-
60031).
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• there is limited overlap between Accenture and Dragos in the
supply of OT cybersecurity services in Australia;
• post-Acquisition, Accenture would continue to face competition
from multiple alternative suppliers of OT cybersecurity services;
• Accenture would be unlikely to have the ability and incentive to
engage in anti-competitive bundling of OT cybersecurity
solutions or otherwise foreclose rivals given the alternative
suppliers of OT cybersecurity services in Australia.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
